summary: Lunar Explorer is an interactive web application built to bring lunar science and NASA’s Artemis exploration to life in any web browser. Using NASA 3D lunar models, surface elevation maps, planetary datasets, and official NASA Goddard mission videos, the platform lets users rotate and zoom a real-time 3D Moon while exploring key lunar metrics and the science behind the Moon’s South Pole. It addresses the challenge of making complex planetary and mission data engaging, visual, and easy to understand without specialized software. This is important because accessible, interactive storytelling helps students, educators, and the public connect with space exploration and understand why returning to the lunar South Pole is vital for future human missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Lunar Explorer is an interactive web application designed to make lunar science and NASA’s Artemis exploration accessible and engaging. Users can explore an interactive 3D lunar globe—rotating and zooming in to inspect surface topography—alongside key planetary metrics (Earth–Moon distance, orbital period, and lunar diameter), curated educational content on why NASA is targeting the Moon’s South Pole for water ice and sustained exploration, and an embedded NASA Goddard educational video.

Benefits & Intended Impact Static textbooks and dense scientific tables often make planetary science feel abstract. By combining real-time 3D visualization with concise mission context and multimedia storytelling, Lunar Explorer helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts intuitively understand lunar geography and the scientific importance of Artemis missions directly in any web browser without needing specialized software.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Frontend Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript (ES6+)
  • 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js (GLTFLoader and OrbitControls) using NASA 3D lunar models (.glb) and surface textures
  • Build & Deployment: Vite for bundling and optimization, and Netlify for live cloud hosting
  • Data & Media: NASA Science lunar datasets, NASA 3D Resources / CGI Moon Kit assets, and NASA Goddard Artemis mission video. Creativity & Design Considerations We designed the interface with a mission-control aesthetic—pairing high-contrast dark-space typography with smooth, responsive 3D controls (OrbitControls) so users feel like they are inspecting a live orbital telemetry feed. Key design factors included optimizing 3D asset loading for smooth browser performance, ensuring responsive layouts across desktop and mobile screens, and organizing complex Artemis South Pole science into clear, digestible visual sections.
